observations: A broad, roughly rectangular head shape sits centered on a flat orange background, outlined in white and filled with overlapping patches of teal, blue, pink, red, and yellow.
Two eye zones each contain a red-and-white crosshatched rectangle, framed by looping black lines; yellow curved strokes cluster beside each eye and below the nose area.
A wide mouth near the bottom holds a row of white rectangular teeth outlined in black, with loose white scribble lines radiating across the top of the head.
reading: The flat orange field pushes the head forward, giving it the blunt presence of a mask rather than a face. Crosshatched red rectangles where eyes would be read as blocked or sealed, while the wide tooth-filled mouth pulls in the opposite direction—open, loud. Layered color patches and white scribble lines sit on top of each other without blending, so the surface feels assembled rather than modeled. The effect is confrontational and a little absurd at once.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #69 and #71. Where #69 uses a muted olive-and-grey palette with long parallel strokes, and #71 strips color to near-monochrome grey and black, #70 is the loudest of the three in both hue and surface density.

connections.reason: Both works share the same flat orange background and a roughly square head with visible teeth and layered scribble lines over color patches; nnotb #168 uses heavier black outlines and a darker interior, making its contrasts starker.
